name: Average Teaching Dimension / Size (square-root upper bound)
details: For every finite binary class $\mathcal H$, $\mathrm{TS}_{\mathrm{avg}}(\mathcal H)=O(\sqrt{|\mathcal H|})$. This nonlinear upper bound is displayed only as a non-constraining graph overlay and does not participate in the Hasse reduction.
proof: Kushilevitz--Linial--Rabinovich--Saks prove that the sum, over the $N=|\mathcal H|$ concepts, of the minimum sizes of their distinguishing witness sets is $O(N^{3/2})$. These witness-set sizes are precisely the individual minimum teaching-set sizes; dividing by $N$ gives the stated average bound.
witness_verification: For #classes/addressing with n>=4, the established endpoint values or bounds, in parameter order, are $1$ and $2^{\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$. The second parameter divided by one plus the first tends to infinity. Thus no reverse affine-linear bound holds. See the database-owned endpoint value proofs.
